title: Bladder muscle holds urine in and can push it out
summary: NIAMS says muscle in the bladder contracts and relaxes to hold urine in or push it out.
body: NIAMS says muscle in the bladder contracts and relaxes so urine is held in or pushed out. A person does not flex it the way an elbow bends. The page files the bladder with other muscle that works on its own. This card is the hold-or-empty job. It does not describe an infection, a test, or a toilet schedule.

sources.title: Health Lesson: Learning About Muscles
sources.author: National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases
